label: accepted

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette read instantly as a scimitar: curved, flaring blade with clipped tip, crescent guard with ball finials, ball pommel; top view is a thin sliver, as expected for any sword, but guard finial still reads.
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: big curved blade, medium crescent guard and ball pommel, small grip bands, finial balls and pommel collar.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised proportions: exaggerated blade flare toward the tip, chunky pommel, swept crescent guard; nothing reads as stiff primitives.
evidence.V4: Guard has consistent chamfers that catch a clean highlight line, blade facets and fuller edges read crisply; pommel collar rim is the only slightly hard-looking edge.
evidence.V5: Flat-light close-ups are clean and A17/A18 pass, but studio fuller close shows a faint shading smear in the dark fuller band near the lower blade and the pommel sphere outline is visibly faceted.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: gold accent, teal grip hue in two values, steel greys on the blade; colourways swap only the grip hue.
evidence.V7: 2440 tris vs weapon target 2500 (ceiling 4000): at or under target.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, kit gold/steel/teal palette, chamfer scale and smooth shading match the kit weapons.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Tool Handle, origin at grip, CollisionFidelity Hull, CanCollide off when equipped, Massless, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic.

artifacts: faint shading smear in the dark fuller band on the lower blade (studio light only)
faceted outline on the pommel sphere
top_fixes: Add a few segments / smooth the pommel sphere so its outline is round at close range
Clean the normals or add a supporting loop along the fuller's dark band on the lower blade to remove the smear
Add a small chamfer to the pommel collar rim to match the guard bevels
